titre: The Wallon Amendment, or the Republic Adopted Without Being Named
accroche: On January 30, 1875, a monarchist assembly founds the Third Republic by a single vote, without the word Republic appearing as a regime.
contenu_vulgarise:
On January 30, 1875, the National Assembly adopts by 353 votes to 352 an amendment by Henri Wallon, a deputy from the Nord. This one-vote margin is often summed up this way: the Republic was voted in by a single vote. The formula is accurate, but it leaves out what was really at stake that day.

## An Assembly That Was Not Republican

The Chamber elected in February 1871 is overwhelmingly monarchist. Its members cannot agree on the name of a king, and France has been in a provisional regime for four years. Since August 1871, the deputies have given the head of government the title “President of the Republic.” It is this usage that Wallon exploits.

The Republican Édouard Lefebvre de Laboulaye had already proposed a more direct text, which proclaimed the Republic. The Assembly had set it aside as too blunt. Wallon takes the opposite route: proclaim nothing, and merely describe how the president is elected, by the Senate and the Chamber of Deputies meeting together as a National Assembly.

## A Regime Installed by Omission

The amendment nowhere says that France is a Republic. But by organizing the election of a head of state who bears that title, it de facto installs a republican office. The monarchists who vote for it know where they stand, and several rally. The result, 353 votes to 352, rests on this rallying of part of the right. On February 24, 1875, the law on the organization of the Senate is adopted by 435 votes to 234: the assembly has pronounced itself more clearly on the container than it had on the principle.

## What This Changes

The Third Republic is often presented as the product of a frank choice by the people or by an assembly won over to the idea. The Wallon vote tells something else: a regime accepted by default, by deputies who had not found a king and preferred a stopgap formula to a rupture. French constitutional history thus rests on a rarely emphasized fact: the founding text of a regime can avoid naming it, and it is precisely this discretion that gets it voted.

There remains a question the amendment leaves hanging: how long can a “provisional” regime remain provisional before becoming, by sheer duration, simply the regime?

repere.texte: January 30, 1875: the Wallon Amendment is adopted by 353 votes to 352. On February 24, 1875, the law on the Senate prevails by 435 votes to 234.
repere.source: Public Sénat, “The Senate celebrates its 150 years: looking back at the fateful day of January 30, 1875”

carte.punch: In 1875, the Republic is adopted by one vote, without the word Republic being proclaimed.
carte.idee: On January 30, 1875, the Wallon Amendment passes by 353 votes to 352 in a mostly monarchist assembly. It does not proclaim the Republic: it organizes the election of a “President of the Republic,” and it is this discretion that makes it possible to vote for it.

quiz.question: Why was the Wallon Amendment able to win over part of the monarchists?
choix: It restored the principle of a king elected by the Senate and the Chamber
It did not proclaim the Republic, but organized the election of a president
It provided that the president would remain in office for life
It had first been voted on by the electorate, by referendum
quiz.explication: Wallon does not proclaim the Republic: he merely describes the election of a “President of the Republic” by the two chambers meeting together, which lets monarchists without a king vote for it without betraying their camp. There is no king, no lifetime term, no referendum.

quiz_supplementaire.question: By how many votes is the Wallon Amendment adopted on January 30, 1875?
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The Wallon Amendment is adopted by a margin of a single vote, 353 to 352, on January 30, 1875.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What had Deputy Laboulaye proposed before the Wallon Amendment was debated?
choix: A text proposing a king elected for life by the Assembly
A text postponing any decision to a popular referendum
A text directly proclaiming the Republic, rejected as too blunt
A text abolishing the office of President of the Republic
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Laboulaye had proposed a text openly proclaiming the Republic; the Assembly found it too direct and set it aside before Wallon.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does the Assembly vote on February 24, 1875, after the Wallon Amendment?
choix: The dissolution of the National Assembly, by 300 votes to 290
The restoration of the monarchy, by 400 votes to 150
A new presidential election, by 353 votes to 352
The law on the organization of the Senate, by 435 votes to 234
quiz_supplementaire.explication: On February 24, 1875, the law on the organization of the Senate is adopted by 435 votes to 234, more clearly than the Wallon Amendment.
